chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, like an idol worshipper.'

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ: The habitual or frequent doer of something

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a theological and ethical link between the habitual consumption of wine (khamr) and the state of idolatry (shirk), teaching that the regular drinker meets Allah in a state comparable to an idol worshipper. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted not merely as a metaphor but as a spiritual reality where the loss of reason through intoxication mirrors the loss of divine guidance in polytheism. The chain of transmission highlights the direct link between the Prophet and Imam al-Sadiq, reinforcing the authority of this classification in fiqh and theology.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd Al Hashaam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The habitual (drinker of) the wine would meet Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic like an idol worshipper’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir from abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘A wine addict will meet Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, as a worshipper of idols will do.’”
